transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (CTO, Solaris Intelligence), Ethan Cole (ML Lead), Priya Nair (Infra)

Summary:
Solaris Intelligence is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployments. Primary evaluation criteria: model selection (open models vs private variants), context length (up to 750k tokens in some workflows but typical 8k-32k), multilingual support (en, es, fr, de, ja), tool-calling/function-calling support, and latency/cost tradeoffs. They want benchmarks with their prompts and a clear pricing comparison for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Topics: model context length, multilingual performance, tool-calling, quantization/throughput, networking (VPC/on-prem), security (SOC2/KMS), benchmarks and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on this account, with Jordan our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya: Hey thanks, doing well. Excited to dig into this — we are trying to figure out which hosting option and which open models make sense for our product.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Real quick can I confirm the primary use cases? From our brief it's customer-facing summarization and a developer tool that needs function-calling for database lookups and multi-turn chat. Anything else?
[00:22] Ethan: Yep that's right. Also we have an internal analytics pipeline that runs longer context analysis — some jobs need >64k context for full docs, but most chat traffic is 8k to 32k.
[00:31] Priya: And from infra we need clarity on VPC support, key management, and if we can do an on-prem box for certain regulated customers.
[00:38] Avery: Perfect. Today we'll focus on model selection: open model comparisons, context length fit, multilingual, and tool-calling support. Jordan will walk through benchmarks and runtime trade-offs.

[01:02] Jordan: Thanks. So high level: Redwood Hosted gives you immediate access to our curated open-model catalog — we have optimized runtimes for Mistral, Llama-family variants, and several community weights. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and better tail-latency guarantees. Private (VPC/on-prem) is what you'd pick if you need full network isolation and your own key management.

[01:35] Maya: For the models themselves — we're interested in larger context models and strong multilingual. We noticed Llama 3 and some Mistral variants support long context, but we're not sure about tool-calling. Does Redwood support that?
[01:47] Jordan: Yes, we support function/tool-calling at the platform level for models that expose the interface. On our runtime we map function calls to a structured output and you can configure safety/validation hooks. There are some model-specific caveats — older weights may not have function signature support out-of-the-box and we sometimes need to wrap with a light adapter.

[02:13] Ethan: Is that adapter automatic? I don't want to hand-roll wrappers for 5 different models.
[02:18] Jordan: We provide adapters for common open models; for edge cases we can supply a sample adapter. The adapter is usually a small shim that translates model tokens into function call JSON. It's not ideal but it's quick.

[03:01] Maya: On context length, we have a few workflows that need 100k-200k tokens — is that realistic on Redwood, or do we need a hybrid approach?
[03:11] Jordan: Long context at 100k+ is possible but comes with cost and latency tradeoffs. We have sequence-chunking and KV cache approaches; for extremely long documents we recommend preprocessing (summarization + retrieval) or using our longer-context model families that are optimized for chunked attention. Dedicated or Private usually gives more predictable throughput for those heavy jobs.

[03:45] Priya: Can you expand on KV cache — sometimes our infra team says K-V cache and sometimes K B cache, what's the difference?
[03:53] Jordan: (laughs) KV cache, key-value. Sorry if transcripts mix that up — it's the model's attention cache to avoid recomputing earlier tokens. Works well for chat and streaming, reduces compute for repeated prefixes. We also do prefix caching at the routing layer.

[04:18] Ethan: Multilingual — how do the open models compare? We need high quality en/es/fr/de/ja, and good low-resource languages for support tickets.
[04:28] Jordan: Mistral 7B-class variants are solid for European languages at lower cost; Llama 3/4 variants and XLM-adapted weights tend to do better for non-western languages. Our evals show Mistral++ is strong for en/es/fr; for ja and lower-resource languages we recommend finetuned or LLMs with explicit multilingual pretraining. We'll share per-model language benchmarks.

[05:00] Maya: Competitors — we've also talked to OpenAI and Anthropic. How should we think about cost and control?
[05:07] Avery: OpenAI gives turnkey quality but at a higher unit cost and less control. Anthropic is similar. With Redwood you get the control to pick models, run quantized weights for volume, and choose Dedicated or Private for SLAs and data residency. So the tradeoff is more ops control vs managed simplicity.

[05:35] Ethan: About quantization — do you support int8 / 4-bit quant? We need best throughput for our bulk inference.
[05:42] Jordan: We support multiple quant profiles — int8, 4-bit, and newer quant formats depending on model compatibility. Quantization cuts memory and cost, sometimes with small quality regressions. We'll recommend per-model quant profiles based on your evals.

[06:08] Priya: Security questions: SOC 2? KMS/HSM? Audit logs? SSO?
[06:12] Avery: Yes — Redwood has SOC 2, supports customer-managed KMS, integrates with common IdP for SSO (SAML/OIDC), and we provide detailed audit logs in the Console. For Private we can support HSM-based key management on-prem if needed. We'll send the security pack after the call.

[06:38] Maya: Great. For the benchmark, we want to test: 1) chat latency under p95 and p99, 2) long-context summarization throughput, and 3) function-calling correctness with our DB layer.

[06:50] Jordan: That lines up with our standard plan. Can you share a sample of the prompt set and the target SLA (p95?) and expected concurrency?

[06:59] Ethan: p95 target 250ms for short chat (under 1k tokens), p99 under 800ms; concurrency is 50-100 sustained with spike to 300. For long-context jobs we expect higher latency and are OK with best-effort as long as throughput is predictable.

[07:20] Jordan: Those are useful numbers. Hosted will be easier to start with for iterative testing but Dedicated is likely necessary to meet consistent p99 during spikes.

[08:05] Maya: Pricing — can you ballpark Hosted vs Dedicated costs for our expected volume?

[08:11] Avery: We'll send a TCO spreadsheet but rough guide: Hosted per-token pricing is flexible but can be higher for large volume. Dedicated gives reserved capacity — pay for reserved GPU hours plus lower per-token usage. Private has a platform fee plus infra. We'll tailor numbers to your traffic profile.

[08:39] Ethan: How much work to move from Hosted trial to Dedicated or Private?

[08:44] Jordan: The API is consistent across modes. Moving is mostly an infra change: re-pointing endpoints, configuring routing and canary rollout. For Private we do an onboarding runbook and a short install window. We can help with migration — it's usually a few weeks depending on procurement and infra.

[09:20] Priya: About networking for Private: can you explain the VPC peering options and if we can keep control of egress?

[09:27] Jordan: We support VPC peering and private link options. You maintain control of egress; audit logs and network policies can be configured. For on-prem we'll coordinate with your infra team on firewall rules.

[10:00] Maya: Any gotchas around tool-calling with open models? We've seen hallucinations when models fabricate DB field names.

[10:09] Jordan: Good point. We add validation and strict schema enforcement for function-calling. You can set a validation layer that rejects anything not matching your schema, and we support sandboxed dry-runs to test the call flow. Also, using model ensembles or reranking can reduce hallucination risk.

[10:45] Ethan: For the long-context models you mentioned chunked attention — is that something we need to do at app layer or does Redwood runtime handle it?

[10:53] Jordan: Our runtime can handle chunking patterns for supported models; otherwise we recommend a retrieval+compose pattern at the app layer. We'll propose architecture options in the benchmark doc.

[11:18] Maya: We care about multilingual scoring. Can you run BLEU/chrF for ja and rouge for en?

[11:25] Jordan: Absolutely — we'll include multilingual evals and specific metrics for each language family. If you have labeled test sets shareable that helps.

[12:05] Priya: One infrastructure constraint: some of our customers require air-gapped deployments for regulated data. Is that feasible?

[12:12] Avery: Yes — for very regulated customers we have an on-prem package that can be air-gapped. That is subject to enterprise licensing and a longer onboarding. We'll attach the on-prem runbook.

[12:40] Ethan: Regarding model freshness — how quickly can we onboard a new open-weight or custom fine-tune?

[12:47] Jordan: Typically we can onboard a community weight in days for Hosted; Dedicated/Private onboarding depends on infra but generally 1-2 weeks for common weights. For custom fine-tunes it's longer — depends on training infra and tests.

[13:18] Maya: For evaluation, we want a shortlist of 3 models to test: one cost-optimized, one balanced, one high-quality. Can Redwood recommend?

[13:27] Jordan: Yes. For your profile I'd suggest: 1) Cost-optimized: Mistral-7B quantized profile; 2) Balanced: Llama-3-13B tuned variant; 3) High-quality / long-context: Llama-3-70B long-context or an XLM-long variant. We'll tune quant and batch profiles per-model.

[14:02] Ethan: Any concerns with tokenization across languages? We have mixed en/ja prompts.

[14:08] Jordan: Tokenization differences can change cost and latency; we'll run tokenizer probes and show expected token counts for your sample prompts. For mixed-language prompts sometimes a multilingual tokenizer is best; we'll include guidance.

[14:45] Maya: For function-calling latency, do you do batching of calls or are they synchronous?

[14:52] Jordan: Calls are synchronous from the model side, but you can batch upstream DB lookups and we support async callbacks to reduce perceived latency. We'll demonstrate patterns in the demo.

[15:20] Priya: On observability, can we get per-route token cost and SLO dashboards?

[15:25] Avery: Yes — Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, traces, and error rates. We can give demo access to your team.

[16:00] Ethan: About fallbacks — if a Dedicated pool is saturated do you fallback to Hosted?

[16:06] Jordan: We have smart routing policies that can fallback to compatible model variants or Hosted pools; you can set policy preferences for cost vs latency vs availability.

[16:40] Maya: For procurement, we need an enterprise agreement for Dedicated and an SOW for Private. What's the typical timeline?

[16:47] Avery: Once scope is agreed it takes ~2-4 weeks for procurement and legal, then provisioning can begin. For Private there's additional lead time for on-prem packaging.

[17:15] Jordan: Quick note on cost savings — prefix caching and batching often reduce per-token compute by 20-50% depending on workload. That can be a big lever for you.

[17:42] Ethan: Great. For the benchmark plan, do you need any infra keys or can you use synthetic traffic?

[17:48] Jordan: Synthetic traffic is fine for initial runs but for function-calling correctness we want your sample dataset. For long-context tests we'd prefer real doc shapes.

[18:30] Maya: Are there rate limits we should be aware of during the trial?

[18:35] Avery: We give generous test quotas. Hosted has rate limits but they're adjustable; Dedicated has reserved throughput. We'll detail this in the onboarding doc.

[19:05] Ethan: Regarding model updates — if an open model gets an upstream update how does Redwood handle versioning?

[19:11] Jordan: We version models and you pin to specific versions. We support canary rollouts when switching. We don't auto-upgrade without explicit migration.

[19:45] Maya: Any specific recommendations for our use case (chat + long context + tool-calling + multilingual)?

[19:52] Jordan: Start Hosted to iterate quickly with the cost-optimized Mistral profile for chat, run dedicated benchmarks with the Llama-3-13B tuned variant for balanced latency, and test the long-context Llama-3-70B (or XLM-long) on Dedicated or Private for heavy jobs. If you need air-gapped or strict KMS, move to Private for those customers.

[20:30] Priya: One last infra question: how are keys rotated in Private?

[20:34] Avery: In Private you control KMS and we integrate with your rotation policy. For Hosted we support customer-managed KMS so you can rotate keys as needed.

[21:00] Jordan: We'll follow up with a benchmark plan, security docs, pricing spreadsheet, and a demo slot focused on function-calling.

[21:20] Maya: Sounds good. For the demo could you show the adapter flow and an example where validation rejects a bad call?

[21:27] Jordan: Yep we'll include a live example and a recorded run for reproducibility.

[22:05] Avery: Quick recap and next steps: Avery will send pricing and security pack, Jordan will send benchmark plan and shortlist of three models plus quant profiles, Ethan will share sample prompts and traffic profile, Priya will confirm VPC/on-prem constraints. We'll target a follow-up demo on 2027-01-28.

[22:32] Maya: Thanks everyone. One note: our legal needs a data flow diagram showing what leaves our VPC for Hosted trials.

[22:40] Avery: We'll include that in the security pack.

[22:58] (crosstalk)
[23:05] Ethan: Ok thanks, we'll collate the prompts and ping you.
[23:12] Priya: Appreciate it, bye.
[23:15] Jordan: Thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
